content:
Start by blocking any antivirus scanning of on access or change in the Thunderbird profile folder. It has a very long history of causing data loss, file corruption and is generally a poor idea.

Personally I dumped paid antivirus for windows defender years ago and have had no virus issues nor related email issues caused by the antivirus product since. I see it as a win win.

It is entirely possible that simply displaying the email sees your antivirus blocking the local temp folder while it scans it. Display of an email almost always included at least one temp file. You might also want to consider a manual cleanup of the temp folder as windows makes no attempt to clean this itself by default and it is a primary cause of the old stories that do the rounds of the internet suggesting Windows gradually slows down after it is installed. The temp folder becomes so full of junk Windows noticeably slows down navigating the tens of thousands of orphaned entries and other oddities appear as a result.

Microsoft offer instructions on how to automate cleanup and how to initiate it manually here https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/learning-center/how-to-delete-temporary-files

This is a known bug. It will be fixed in TB158.0 to be released next week. https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2077526

Beyond drag and drop there is another workaround:

  • at the top right of the Thunderbird window, click the menu button ≡ > Settings > General
  • scroll down to the bottom and click 'Config Editor'
  • search for the preference mail.compose.attach.dir
  • the value (Path) here must be changed to one that is still available (for example C:)
  • restart Thunderbird

That should fix it.

content:
This is a recently discovered bug. The symptom is that, if you previously attached a file but the previous containing folder now no longer exists because it was deleted or renamed, when you later try to attach a file using the Write window's "Attach" button, it will silently fail. That is, clicking the button will appear to do nothing. The bug should be fixed in the next release.

In the meantime, a workaround is to drag-and-drop the file onto the Write window using the mouse.

Or, if you don't mind changing Thunderbird's Advanced Settings:

- In <Settings | General | Config Editor> search for: "mail.compose.attach.dir".

- The value (path) here must be changed to one that is still available (for example C:\).

- Close and exit Thunderbird, then restart it (this step might not be necessary.)
